# Scope notes

- All pages were read on 2026-11-12. `developers.openai.com/codex` now redirects (HTTP 308) to `learn.chatgpt.com/docs`, a documentation set that combines ChatGPT and Codex. Pages switch content by surface (app, web, CLI, IDE). I rated what a page states for the Codex surfaces (desktop app, CLI, IDE extension, Codex Cloud).
- The same documentation set covers "dots" (a separate product in this study) and ChatGPT Work, Space and Enterprise "teams". I did not count dots features. I counted a ChatGPT-wide feature only where the page says it applies to Codex, and I say so in the cell.
- URLs below are the page URLs; each also has a Markdown twin at the same URL plus `.md`, which is what I fetched.
- Availability words are the vendor's (stable, beta, experimental, preview) from the page or from `codex features list`.

# The 25 services

| Service | Value | Quote | URL | Availability and reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Harness | **yes** | "Let Codex inspect files, make edits, and run the tools already installed on your machine." Also: "Codex replaces earlier turns with a concise summary, freeing context while keeping critical details." | https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli | Stable. Codex runs the agent loop, manages context (compaction) and executes tool calls. |
| Sessions | **yes** | "Codex reloads the selected chat's transcript so you can pick up where you left off, keeping the original history intact." Also: "By default, Codex saves local session transcripts under `CODEX_HOME`" and (`/app`) "The desktop app opens the same saved chat so you can continue there." | https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-advanced | Stable. `codex resume`, `fork`, `archive`, `delete` in the CLI help; saved transcripts remain after the work ends. |

A goal keeps the request and can be paused, resumed or cleared, and cloud tasks have an id and status. I found no statement that Codex coordinates retry or recovery of a task. Yes is defensible because tracking, cancellation and the kept request are all stated. |

Event triggers are stated for ChatGPT web and mobile only, and the only stated concurrency limit is for subagents ("Maximum number of spawned-agent threads that can be open concurrently, excluding the primary thread."). Counts: 14 yes, 11 part (7 of them DISPUTABLE toward yes), 0 no, 0 not assessed.

# Four further questions

## 1. Areas of work (C1 to C4, rerate-criteria-v2)

**C1. An area of work exists in the model: part, DISPUTABLE (yes).**
Quote: "A group of related chats and shared sources, or a local folder used for file-based work." (glossary entry "Project", https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/glossary). Also: "Use a project to keep related chats, files, instructions, and sources together." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/projects).
Reason: the only unit above a single agent in Codex's own model is the project. It is defined, several can exist side by side, and many chats and agents work in one. It is defined as a container of chats and files (in the CLI, the directory where Codex starts), not as an area of work or organizational unit, so I give part. Yes is defensible because projects do divide a system's work into more than one area. The combined documentation also describes Enterprise "teams" ("Teams can include people within a department or across functions who share a goal.", https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/teams); that page presents teams as a ChatGPT workspace feature and does not mention Codex, so I did not count it. The glossary has no entry for domain, department, team or organization.

**C2. The area is specified apart from who does the work: part.**
Quote: "To define your own custom agents, add standalone TOML files under `~/.codex/agents/` for personal agents or `.codex/agents/` for project-scoped agents." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents). Glossary, "Custom agent": "User-defined agent role with its own instructions and settings."
Reason: at the level of the project the pages specify rules (project instructions, `AGENTS.md`, project configuration) and roles (project-scoped custom agents, defined apart from the threads that fill them). They do not specify what the project as a whole is responsible for. That meets (b) and not (a).

**C3. A record of accountability: part.**
Quote: "Each token belongs to its creator and that user's ChatGPT workspace. Tokens act as agent identities for programmatic local workflows." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/access-tokens).
Reason: the workspace keeps a list of access tokens and service accounts, each with an owner. That names a responsible person per agent identity. No record names one accountable area or owner per responsibility or capability. Searched: the documentation export for "accountab", "owner", "responsib", "directory", "registry", "catalog".

**C4. Finding where to send work: part.**
Quote: "Role guidance shown to Codex when choosing and spawning that agent type." (`agents.<name>.description`, https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference). Also: "Human-facing guidance for when Codex should use this agent." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents).
Reason: the spawning agent sees the list of agent roles with a description of when to use each and reaches one by spawning it. The routing lives in that one agent's prompt; there is no lookup service that any agent can ask.

Derived Directory: part.

## 2. Supplied agents for an area of work

All supplied items are for software development or software security. None found for any other named area of work (searched the documentation index, the plugins page, the build-skills page and the use-cases page; the use-cases page offers example workflows filtered by team such as Finance, Marketing and Sales, which are prompts, not supplied agents).

- Built-in agents: "Codex ships with built-in agents:" `default` ("general-purpose fallback agent."), `worker` ("execution-focused agent for implementation and fixes."), `explorer` ("read-heavy codebase exploration agent."). https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents
- Codex Security plugin, CLI and SDK: "Install the Codex Security plugin to scan authorized code and confirm plausible vulnerability findings." https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/plugins ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/security
- Code Review plugin: "The Code Review plugin shows a pull request's description, changed files, comments, and checks." https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/code-review
- System skills (for building skills, not for an area of work): "Includes `skill-creator` and `skill-installer`. Enabled by default." Curated skills can be added: "To add curated skills beyond the built-ins for your own local Codex setup, use `$skill-installer`." (the page's example is `$linear`). https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills
- Plugins that connect a tool rather than supply an agent for an area: Gmail, Google Drive, Slack. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/plugins

## 3. What fits nowhere

- Usage metering, credits and spend controls: "ChatGPT workspace usage limits and spend controls apply to eligible activity under your workspace plan, which can include some Codex activity." https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/usage-limits . In the CLI, `/usage`: "Codex opens usage actions or shows account token activity for the selected view." https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli . The Scheduling service limits how much runs at once, not what it costs.
- Hosting what the agent builds for outside visitors: "Sites lets you build, host, and share a website by describing it in ChatGPT or Codex." https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sites . The Artifacts service covers storing the page and its versions; serving it to an audience with sign-in, a database and analytics is not in any of the 25.
- Importing a setup from another vendor's agent: "Use the import flow to bring instructions, settings, skills, plugins, projects, and recent work from another agent into the ChatGPT desktop app or Codex CLI." https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/import
- Capturing the person's own activity as context: "Computer History turns your activity across apps and websites into memories and a timeline that ChatGPT and Codex can reference." https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/customization/computer-history . The Memory service is about what agents learn; this records what the person did. It could also be read as a source for Memory.

## 4. Where it runs and what the user supplies

**Where the agent runs: both.** "Both **Local** and **Worktree** chats run on your computer." and "**Cloud**: run a remote task in its own workspace." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/modes). The repository README says Codex CLI "is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer." (https://github.com/openai/codex).

**Does it keep running when the user is away?** In the cloud, yes: "Each task has its own workspace and can keep working while your computer is asleep." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud). On the user's machine, only while that machine and the app stay on: "For project-scoped scheduled tasks, keep the machine powered on and the ChatGPT desktop app running." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/automations). The CLI has no scheduler ("Codex CLI doesn't provide the Scheduled management interface."). A task is a bounded piece of work, not a standing agent; I found no standing named Codex agent that stays active between tasks.

**What the user must supply or build for sustained work:**
- A ChatGPT plan or an API key, and for cloud work a prepared environment ("To reuse a setup across tasks, create a reusable environment.", https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/modes).
- The standing instructions: "Keep required team guidance in `AGENTS.md` or checked-in documentation. Treat memories as a helpful recall layer, not as the only source for rules that must always apply." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/customization/memories).
- The roles: "To define your own custom agents, add standalone TOML files under `~/.codex/agents/` for personal agents or `.codex/agents/` for project-scoped agents." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents).
- The recurring work and its stopping rules: "make the prompt durable. It should describe what ChatGPT should do on each scheduled run, how to decide whether there is anything important to report, and when to stop or ask you for input." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/automations).
- Skills for cloud work must be in the repository: "Skills stored in your repository are available in cloud tasks. Personal skills from your local computer aren't synced to cloud environments." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments).
- Anything headless or continuous outside the desktop app's scheduler is built by the user on `codex exec`, the Codex SDK, the app server or the GitHub Action: "Compose with scripts and CI:" (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli); "Use the Codex GitHub Action (`openai/codex-action@v1`) to run Codex in CI/CD jobs, apply patches, or post reviews from a GitHub Actions workflow." (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/github-action).
- Not supplied, so the user builds them: areas of work with stated responsibilities, a record of which area is accountable for what, messaging between independent agents, evaluation of agent behavior, and a release process for agent definitions and rules (see the part cells above).
